scope: The eight actual associated constants, eleven public conversions and five checked 256-bit add/subtract/negation methods with exact integer values and exact Overflow partitions; U256::div_rem and U256::checked_div with exact canonical quotient, rounding and refusal contracts; U256::full_product and U256::checked_mul with exact product contracts; the U512::checked_add, U512::multiply_u256, U512::div_rem and U768::div_rem wrappers; U256::mul_add_div_rem, mul_div, mul_div_half_up, mul3_div and products_ge over complete 512/768-bit products with exact refusal order; and the seven signed I256 multiply, divide, complete-product division, comparison and i128 narrowing methods with exact signed rounding and refusal contracts, all without public input preconditions. The actual negative_bits dependency, the add/subtract carry and borrow helpers, the private divider, word insertion and schoolbook multiplier are refined at every limb width (the multiplier whenever its output has room for the product). U256 has no checked_neg method. The square-root family, the raw wide word views, other arithmetic and compiler/ghost-erasure correspondence are not proved.
assumptions: Soundness of the pinned Verus frontend, vstd specifications and SMT solver.
Correspondence between Rust compilation and the proof frontend, including ghost erasure and the reviewed constant annotations.
Standard Rust fixed-width integer and array semantics as specified by the pinned verifier; native execution is separately tested.

Domain iff any of the six factors is negative; otherwise whether the first triple product is at least the second.
Exact value iff it is in [-2^127,2^127); otherwise exactly Overflow.
